clinician.trajectory_summary: A 55-year-old male with vascular risk factors (hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia) and prior cerebrovascular events (stroke at age 54 with right hemiparesis and micro-ischemic lesions; TIA 6 months prior with transient speech impairment and right arm weakness) presented with 1-year progressive dizziness and gait instability, plus 2-month progressive cognitive decline and low mood. Neurological examination on admission revealed reduced cognitive function (MMSE 21) without acute focal neurological deficits. CTA imaging identified bilateral internal carotid artery kinking with right-sided duplex kinking. SPECT imaging with 99mTc-HMPAO confirmed global cortical hypoperfusion, indicating chronic vascular failure. The patient was treated with dual antiplatelet therapy (acetylsalicylic acid and clopidogrel), statin (atorvastatin), cognitive enhancers (donepezil and memantine), mood stabilizer (escitalopram), anxiolytic (bromazepam), and optimization of antihypertensive and antidiabetic therapy.
